assertions.name: CH₄ (no lone pairs) reproduces the tetrahedral reference
second-row hydrides predicted within ~3° from one derived q² ratio
assertions.source: CH₄/NH₃/H₂O angles from domain counts + the single derived lone/bond = q² ratio; no per-molecule tuning

description: General symmetric-Wedderburn-block bond angles for AX_nE_m hydrides. One DERIVED lone/bond weight ratio q² (trivial-rep q³/q, no central-atom input, no fit) plugged into a weighted points-on-a-sphere VSEPR; molecule variation carried entirely by domain counts (n bonds + m lone pairs). Predicts CH₄/NH₃/H₂O second-row angles; H₂S (third row) deviates as expected. Generalises h2o_angle_q2_symmetric_block.py.

data.finding: The q² lone/bond ratio derived for H₂O generalises: with ONE derived ratio (q²=1.2321) and only the domain counts, the weighted VSEPR predicts the second-row hydride angles CH₄/NH₃/H₂O within 0.2° (CH₄ exact by symmetry). H₂S (third row) misses by +12.6° — the q² second-row electron structure does not capture the heavier-atom, less-hybridised lone-pair effect, which is a separate (honest) correction, not a fit knob.
